Title: Allergic Rhinitis: Ragweed Season Symptom Relief That Actually Works

Description:
Ragweed pollen allergy affects 23 million+ people in the US, and nearly 50 million feel symptoms in late summer and fall — season starts early August and peaks mid-September through October. It happens because your immune system misreads ragweed pollen as a threat and releases histamine, triggering sneezing, runny nose, congestion, and itchy eyes. The local honey myth doesn't hold up (bee pollen and wind-blown ragweed pollen are completely different).

Three things genuinely help: nasal saline irrigation, a HEPA air filter used with realistic expectations, and the right antihistamine (or a prescription nasal steroid if symptoms drag on).
